title: Predestination?
prayer: Lord, you know me more completely than I know myself. Help me freely choose you, especially when I cannot see where my choices are leading. Take even my mistakes and use them for your purpose. Conform my heart more closely to your Son, and when my journey is finished, bring me home to the place you have prepared for me. Amen.
body:
The word *predestined* can trouble us. It can make us wonder whether everything has already been decided—our successes, our failures, even whether we will ultimately belong to God. But perhaps Paul is pointing us toward something much more hopeful.

God knows us. He knows our hearts, our weaknesses, the decisions we will make and the roads we will take. Yet knowing is not the same as choosing for us. We still decide whether to turn toward him, whether to receive his mercy, and whether to allow ourselves to be “conformed to the image of his Son.”

And our choices will not always be perfect. We will take wrong turns. We will misunderstand. We will sometimes choose ourselves before God. Yet even these imperfect pieces of our lives can be taken up by God and woven into his greater purpose.

Maybe that is God's master plan—not some grandiose destiny where every detail of our lives has been scripted beforehand, but a destination already prepared for us. God knows where he wants to bring us: home to him.

The genealogy of Jesus reminds us of this. Generation after generation, through faithful people and deeply flawed people, through good decisions and terrible ones, God's promise continued moving forward until Christ entered the world. Human imperfection did not defeat God's purpose.

And perhaps the same is true of us.

God calls. God knows. God forgives. God redirects. God can use even the crooked roads we have traveled. But he does not force us to love him.

The destination may already be prepared, but we still choose whether to walk toward it.

Perhaps that is the mystery of predestination: not that God has decided our answer, but that long before we answer, **he already knows where his love is trying to lead us.**
